corpus.note: Built with `ccg build $(go env GOMODCACHE)/github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.10.2 --exclude '*_test.go' --exclude site`. No ccg annotations, so the intent index is empty; see the gorm corpus note. Chosen as a second vocabulary — CLI plumbing instead of ORM plumbing — so a constant fitted to either would show on the other.

authorship.written_by: assistant, 2026-08-10, before running any measurement; every judged symbol was verified to exist in the built graph first
authorship.caveat: Same rules as the primary set: expectations are never edited to make a run pass.

queries.why: The variant of Execute that returns the executed command; the trailing C makes it unambiguous.
PersistentFlags split at its case boundary; the accessor is where the persistent flag set lives.
UsageTemplate split at its case boundary.
completions.go holds the shell-agnostic completion engine and the `completion` command; the per-shell generators (bash_completions.go and friends) are acceptable too, but the engine is the answer.
The whole feature is one file: AppendActiveHelp and the environment-variable plumbing.
MarkFlagsRequiredTogether and friends live in flag_groups.go; ValidateFlagGroups is the enforcement point.

The function is named ld, so nothing in its name or path says levenshtein — only its docstring does. This is the docstring-retrieval case: an annotation-free corpus answering a concept word from the comment text.
A CLI framework has none of this. The right answer is nothing.
